messages:
jane-cs: Hey team — customer on Dedicated (private VPC) reporting streaming sessions cut mid-response. They see partial text, client reconnects, then the next chunk starts from beginning (duplicate content). Happening only from their corporate network, works fine from home. They pasted a client trace showing TCP FIN right after a large chunk.

sarah: Thanks, can you paste the root request headers and the raw chunk boundary from their capture? Also confirm whether this is over HTTP/1.1 SSE (text/event-stream) or HTTP/2 streaming.

jane-cs: It's SSE (text/event-stream) over HTTP/1.1 through their corp proxy (they said "BlueFrogProxy" but likely an F5/nginx stack). Root request: `GET /v1/streams/generate HTTP/1.1`, `Accept: text/event-stream`, `Authorization: Bearer <redacted>`, `Connection: keep-alive`, `Cache-Control: no-cache`. Capture snippet they sent: `\n0000: 0b\r\nHello world... (big chunk)\r\n0000: 1e\r\nmore text...\r\n` then `RST` / `FIN` after ~1460 bytes.

liam: MTU-sized behavior — corp proxies or middleboxes often drop or reset on large chunked frames, especially with transparent SSL terminators. If FIN occurs ~1460 bytes that's the typical TCP MSS. Could be PMTU/MTU mismatch or the proxy reassembling and then timing out.

dan: Also seen on-prem reverse proxies that buffer until event end and then flush; if they hit buffer limit they drop connection. Questions: is the server sending large single SSE events (long lines) instead of frequent small events?

jane-cs: Customer said model responses are long (several KB). We do not chunk at application level — the runtime writes tokens as they come but sometimes a single write ends up as a large TCP packet.

tyler: Repro plan: 1) Try reproducing from a host behind a corporate proxy (we have corp-proxy lab). 2) Run curl -N to keep connection open and stream. 3) Simulate large SSE event by sending a single 8KB line from our test app and see whether proxy terminates.

sarah: Also ask customer for proxy vendor/version and whether there's any L7 appliance rewriting `Transfer-Encoding` or performing buffering. Common culprits: `nginx` with `proxy_buffering on`, F5 with HTTP profile `buffer` enabled, or corporate DLP appliances.

liam: If it's MTU-related, quick mitigation is to ensure TCP MSS/MTU path is correct or to reduce application-side write size (force smaller chunks). For SSE, we can force a flush after each token by writing `\n\n` boundaries or sending smaller event frames.

jane-cs: They want a recommended fix that doesn't require changing their corporate proxy. Any server-side or client-side knobs?

tyler: Server-side: we can change runtime to break up large writes into <=1200 byte segments to avoid MSS-edge fragmentation. That's a code-level change and might add CPU overhead. Client-side workaround: set `Connection: keep-alive` + periodic heartbeats (comment: they already have). Also set the client to perform exponential backoff on reconnect and use idempotency keys to avoid billing/duplicate side effects.

dan: Important: duplicate tokens — customer reported seeing duplicated content after reconnect, and worried about billing double-count. Streaming reconnects shouldn't normally be billed twice for the same tokens unless the client re-sends the original request. Confirm billing semantics with the ingest path; we currently bill per token emitted by runtime. If reconnect causes server to re-emit same tokens we need to track per-request resume offsets in server to dedupe — not trivial.

liam: Short-term: advise client to implement a client-side dedupe: if they receive events that exactly match the last N tokens before reconnect, discard duplicates client-side. Also add a unique request-id header our runtime echoes back to correlate.

sarah: I asked dev-runtime to capture an example trace when the connection is closed by a remote RST. Tyler, can you deploy a debug build with `--sse-flush-interval=50ms` and `--max-write-bytes=1200` to a canary to test?

tyler: Yep, canary build pushed to staging. Config snippet used: ```json
{
  "sse_flush_interval_ms": 50,
  "sse_max_write_bytes": 1200,
  "enable_keepalive": true
}
```

ops-bot: deploy job #7241 completed to staging (green).

jane-cs: Customer tested staging URL with `curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" https://staging-redwood/...` from behind their corp proxy — still saw disconnects, but no partial events (they said more graceful drop instead of mid-line truncation).

liam: That suggests our max-write-bytes helped avoid mid-packet truncation. Next: ask them to capture proxy logs around the time of the disconnect. Look for logs mentioning "buffer overflow", "client closed connection", or L7 resets.

jane-cs: They provided an nginx access log entry: `upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream` and `client closed keepalive connection`. Also a syslog line on the proxy: `nginx: *12345 client timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading client request` — interesting, timed out reading client request, not upstream.

dan: Could be the proxy's idle timeout shorter than our long-running streaming responses. What are their proxy's `proxy_read_timeout` / `keepalive_timeout`? If the proxy considers the stream idle between our small writes it may close. Heartbeat frequency matters.

tyler: We should recommend heartbeat event every 15s or less, and for on-prem proxies ask to raise `proxy_read_timeout` to >120s. For corporate proxies that can't be changed, keep flushing data more frequently.

liam: Another angle: some proxies enforce `client_max_body_size` or limit header size and then reset on large headers. Not likely here. Also check for TLS termination re-handles that accidentally re-negotiate and break TCP.

jane-cs: Customer also asked if we can detect a proxy reset and automatically retry server-side so client sees continuous stream — any risk of double-emit?

dan: Risky. A server-side automatic retry would likely re-run the model or re-emit tokens. Without a resume token or deterministic checkpointing we can't safely resume mid-stream. We need client-side reconnect with dedupe, or implement resumable streaming (track token offsets per request id and allow clients to request resume-from-offset). That is a roadmap item.

sarah: Action items: 1) Advise customer to enable frequent heartbeats (<=15s) or increase proxy timeouts. 2) Suggest client dedupe + idempotency header. 3) We're shipping canary with small-write flushes; watch canary metrics for CPU and latency impact. 4) Ask customer for proxy vendor/version and packet captures. 5) Longer term: investigate resumable-streaming feature.

jane-cs: I'll send the suggested config and the canary link. They asked for a short troubleshooting checklist they can hand to their networking team — can we provide one?

tyler: Draft checklist (send to customer):
- Confirm proxy vendor/version and TLS termination point.
- Ensure `proxy_read_timeout` / idle timeouts >= 120s for streaming endpoints.
- Disable aggressive buffering for streaming endpoints (`proxy_buffering off` for nginx, F5 HTTP profile `buffer` off).
- If MTU/mss issues suspected, test with lowered MTU (e.g., 1420) on a host behind the proxy.
- Allow `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and avoid L7 reassembly policies.
- Capture `tcpdump`/PCAP showing FIN/RST packets and the last few bytes before reset.

liam: Also include a quick curl reproduction they can run: ```bash
curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://<host>/v1/streams/generate?simulate_long_event=1"
```
This `simulate_long_event` is our staging debug endpoint to test large single-event payload behavior.

jane-cs: Customer ran that and attached PCAP — showed an intermediate device sending `RST, ACK` immediately after a 1460-byte burst. I'll forward to the networking team.

dan: Good. For the ticket: mark severity as P2 (customer impact but workaround exists). Add note to billing: no double-charge expected from reconnects in this case (we only bill tokens actually generated); however, if client replays request they may incur more tokens. Recommend client dedupe to be safe.

sarah: I'll update the ticket with the checklist, staging canary link, and request for proxy logs + pcap. Keep thread updated.

jane-cs: Thanks everyone — I'll follow up once networking team replies. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Ticket #T-93421 updated, watcher: @sarah, @tyler, @liam.
